title: Right-horn filtration of boundary prisms
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns and degreewise products of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and colimits of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Put $\partial\Delta^m=\bigcup_{a=0}^m d_a\Delta^{m-1}$ for $m\geq1$, and $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. For every integer $m\geq0$ there are simplicial subsets
$$ X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq X_{m+1}=\Delta^1\times\Delta^m $$
with $X_0=(\{1\}\times\Delta^m)\cup(\Delta^1\times\partial\Delta^m)$, such that, for each $0\leq q\leq m$, the square with top row $\Lambda_{q+1}^{m+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{m+1}$ and bottom row $X_q\hookrightarrow X_{q+1}$ is a pushout. The composite of the right vertical map with $X_{q+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1\times\Delta^m$ is $\sigma_q:\Delta^{m+1}\to\Delta^1\times\Delta^m$, with vertices $\sigma_q(j)=(0,j)$ for $j\leq q$ and $\sigma_q(j)=(1,j-1)$ for $j>q$; the left vertical map is its restriction to the horn. Moreover $X_{q+1}=X_q\cup\operatorname{im}(\sigma_q)$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2.12 (00TH), assertions (a) and (b) and the explicit sigma maps in its proof; this is the boundary-prism input of Proposition 4.2.5.3. Kerodon tag, not the unrelated Stacks tag; read online, archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Fix $m\geq0$. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], an $r$-simplex of $\Delta^1\times\Delta^m$ is a pair of weakly increasing maps, equivalently a weak chain in $\{0,1\}\times\{0,\ldots,m\}$. The ordered list $V_q=((0,0),\ldots,(0,q),(1,q),\ldots,(1,m))$ is a strictly increasing chain with $m+2$ entries. Postcomposition with this list defines the specified $\sigma_q$, because it commutes with precomposition. Its entries are distinct, so it is injective in every degree. Its image consists exactly of chains whose vertices belong to $V_q$: the positions of those vertices give the unique weakly increasing preimage.

source.place: Kerodon Lemma 3.1.2.12 (00TH), proof; explicit degreewise details supplied by Q70. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag.

proof.text: Define $X_0$ as in the statement and recursively set $X_{q+1}=X_q\cup\operatorname{im}(\sigma_q)$. Each is a simplicial subset: precomposition preserves membership in each image, in the terminal endpoint, and in the boundary, and preserves unions. Thus $X_q=X_0\cup\bigcup_{p<q}\operatorname{im}(\sigma_p)$. In the chain description of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], a chain is in $\Delta^1\times\partial\Delta^m$ exactly when its second coordinates omit some element of $\{0,\ldots,m\}$. For $m=0$ no nonempty chain does so, agreeing with the prescribed empty boundary.

source.place: Kerodon Lemma 3.1.2.12 (00TH), proof; explicit degreewise details supplied by Q70. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag.

proof.text: Every chain belongs to some $\operatorname{im}(\sigma_q)$. If it has no vertex with first coordinate $0$, take $q=0$. Otherwise let $q$ be the largest second coordinate among its vertices with first coordinate $0$. All such vertices have second coordinate at most $q$; all vertices with first coordinate $1$ have second coordinate at least $q$, by monotonicity of the original chain. All its vertices therefore lie in $V_q$, and the unique positions in $V_q$ give its preimage. This argument allows repeated vertices and chains with no first coordinate $1$. Consequently $X_{m+1}=\Delta^1\times\Delta^m$.

source.place: Kerodon Lemma 3.1.2.12 (00TH), proof; explicit degreewise details supplied by Q70. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag.

proof.text: Fix $q$ and consider each face $d_j\Delta^m\subseteq\Delta^{m+1}$ for $j\ne q+1$. If $j<q$, deleting the $j$th vertex of $V_q$ omits second coordinate $j$; if $j>q+1$, it omits second coordinate $j-1$. Those faces map into the boundary part of $X_0$. The remaining face is $j=q$. For $q=0$ it has only vertices with first coordinate $1$, so maps into the endpoint part of $X_0$. For $q>0$, its vertices are $(0,0),\ldots,(0,q-1),(1,q),\ldots,(1,m)$, all belonging to $V_{q-1}$, so it maps into $\operatorname{im}(\sigma_{q-1})\subseteq X_q$. The horn is the union of precisely these faces, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Hence $\Lambda_{q+1}^{m+1}\subseteq\sigma_q^{-1}X_q$.

source.place: Kerodon Lemma 3.1.2.12 (00TH), proof; explicit degreewise details supplied by Q70. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag.

proof.text: Conversely, an $r$-simplex $t:[r]\to[m+1]$ outside $\Lambda_{q+1}^{m+1}$ contains every vertex other than possibly $q+1$, by the horn definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Thus $\sigma_qt$ contains $(0,0),\ldots,(0,q)$ and $(1,q+1),\ldots,(1,m)$. Its second coordinates cover all of $\{0,\ldots,m\}$, so it is outside the boundary part of $X_0$. It contains $(0,q)$, so it is outside the terminal endpoint, and outside every $\operatorname{im}(\sigma_p)$ with $p<q$, whose vertices with first coordinate $0$ have second coordinate at most $p$. Therefore it is outside $X_q$. This proves the exact degreewise identity $\sigma_q^{-1}X_q=\Lambda_{q+1}^{m+1}$, including all degenerate simplices.

source.place: Kerodon Lemma 3.1.2.12 (00TH), proof; explicit degreewise details supplied by Q70. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag.

proof.text: Verify the pushout directly using the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Given any simplicial set $T$ and maps $f:X_q\to T$ and $g:\Delta^{m+1}\to T$ agreeing after restriction to the horn, define $h:X_{q+1}\to T$ in each degree by $h(x)=f(x)$ for $x\in X_q$ and $h(\sigma_q(t))=g(t)$ on the image of $\sigma_q$. Injectivity of $\sigma_q$ makes the second rule unambiguous; Step 5 and the agreement on the horn make the two rules agree on their overlap. For a simplicial operator, both subsets are stable and each rule commutes with that operator because $f,g,\sigma_q$ are simplicial. Hence $h$ is a simplicial map. It is unique since these two subsets cover $X_{q+1}$. This is the required pushout, with its maps exactly the horn restriction of $\sigma_q$ and $\sigma_q$ itself. The recursive definition, the endpoint computation, and Step 3 give every remaining clause. In particular at $m=0$ this is the attachment of $\Delta^1$ along $\Lambda_1^1=\{1\}$ to $X_0=\{1\}$.
